data.source_title: Measurement Error Due to Patient Flow in Estimates of Intensive Care Unit Length of Stay
data.locator: Results, paragraph beginning 'From the administrative data'; Web Table 2
data.source_setting: Medical ICU, Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.
data.source_period: Calendar years 2010–2012 for administrative MICU discharges; separate SUNSET-ICU trial-participant analysis, trial period not specified in this extract.
data.source_n: 3,851 MICU discharges for administrative analysis; Web Table 2 reports 1,149 MICU discharges among SUNSET-ICU trial participants.
data.quantity: Median time from observed discharge readiness to actual MICU discharge (immutable time), administrative cohort
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed administrative timestamps summarized by the authors; median and quartiles are measured site distributions, not modeled values.
data.limitations: Single academic MICU, historical 2010–2012 period, and endpoint is readiness-to-actual-departure interval rather than environmental bed-cleaning time alone. The paper calls this interval immutable time and cautions that ICU length of stay can incorporate post-readiness flow delays.
data.inferred_scenario_use: External proxy only: a scenario may vary a post-readiness ICU bed-occupancy delay around this reported distribution, with a separate local-calibration parameter. Do not transfer as a target-site estimate or assume all delay is caused by ward-bed unavailability.

data.source_title: Measurement Error Due to Patient Flow in Estimates of Intensive Care Unit Length of Stay
data.locator: Results, Secondary data analysis, paragraph reporting the 1,149 SUNSET-ICU discharges; the text reports the 5.1-hour median and IQR and points to Web Table 2 for percentiles. Article period is specified in Methods, Secondary data analysis.
data.source_setting: Medical ICU, Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States; trial-participant subset.
data.source_period: SUNSET-ICU MICU cohort, September 12, 2011 to September 11, 2012; ICU readmissions excluded.
data.source_n: 1,149 MICU discharges to another hospital unit or ward among SUNSET-ICU trial participants.
data.quantity: Median time from discharge readiness to actual discharge in SUNSET-ICU subset
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed readiness and discharge timestamps among trial participants; author-reported distribution.
data.limitations: Single academic MICU and trial cohort. The main Results text directly reports median 5.1 h, IQR 2.7–8.9 h, 90th percentile 14.2 h, and 95th percentile 21.7 h, citing Web Table 2; the supplementary table itself was not separately opened. Keep this cohort separate from the 2010–2012 administrative series.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as a lower/alternate external scenario for post-readiness transfer delay; preserve separate from the 2010–2012 administrative distribution and calibrate to local timestamp definitions.

data.source_title: Measurement Error Due to Patient Flow in Estimates of Intensive Care Unit Length of Stay
data.source_setting: Medical ICU, Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed timestamp distribution summarized by authors; request times concentrated in the hour of morning bed-management rounds.
data.limitations: Single MICU workflow; reported as more than half, without an exact percentage in the article text. This is request timing, not completed transfer timing or a universal discharge schedule.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Can motivate a sensitivity scenario with clustered morning ICU transfer requests, while keeping local request timing unknown until measured.
